headline.title: Nemotron 3.5 Content Safety: Customizable Multimodal Safety for Global Enterprise AI
headline.summary: Nemotron 3.5 introduces customizable multimodal safety features designed to enhance content safety for global enterprise AI applications. This update aims to provide organizations with tailored solutions to manage and mitigate risks associated with AI-generated content.

articles.title: What to expect from WWDC 2026: Siri’s highly anticipated revamp and Apple Intelligence updates
articles.summary: Apple's WWDC 2026 is expected to showcase a significant revamp of Siri and updates to Apple Intelligence features. The event will highlight advancements in AI technology and user experience enhancements across Apple's ecosystem.

articles.title: Kevin O’Leary agrees to downsize massive Utah data center
articles.summary: Kevin O'Leary has agreed to reduce the size of his proposed 40,000-acre data center in Utah by nearly half, following concerns raised by local residents and activists. The decision involves removing 19,430 acres from the initial project plan, as communicated in a letter to Utah Senate President J. Stuart Adams.

articles.title: The AI IPO Race Heats Up, DOGE Whistleblower Sues Elon Musk, and Instagram Gets Hacked
articles.summary: Top AI companies are gearing up for initial public offerings (IPOs), with some real estate listings now accepting Anthropic stock as payment. In other news, a whistleblower has filed a lawsuit against Elon Musk related to DOGE, and Instagram has experienced a security breach.

articles.title: Apple touts $1.4 trillion in App Store billings and sales, 90% without a commission
articles.summary: Apple's App Store reported $1.4 trillion in billings and sales, an increase from $1.3 trillion the previous year, with $149 billion attributed to digital goods. Notably, 90% of these transactions occurred without incurring a commission.

articles.title: Dreaming: Better memory for a more helpful ChatGPT
articles.summary: ChatGPT has implemented a new memory system designed to enhance its ability to remember user preferences and maintain context throughout interactions. This update aims to improve the overall user experience by making conversations more relevant and personalized.

articles.title: How courts are coping with a flood of AI-generated lawsuits
articles.summary: Federal magistrate judges, like Maritza Braswell in Colorado, are increasingly handling a surge of AI-generated lawsuits filed by individuals who often lack legal representation. These cases typically involve plaintiffs who cannot afford a lawyer or whose claims are considered too weak or minor for legal counsel to take on.

articles.title: Is Silicon Valley ready to put robots in people’s homes? Hello Robot is.
articles.summary: California startup Hello Robot has launched the fourth generation of its home assistance robot, Stretch, aimed at integrating robotic technology into everyday household tasks. The new model is designed to enhance home automation and support users in various domestic activities.

articles.title: EVA-Bench Data 2.0: 3 Domains, 121 Tools, 213 Scenarios
articles.summary: EVA-Bench Data 2.0 has been released, featuring 121 tools across three domains and 213 scenarios to aid in the evaluation of AI models. This updated dataset aims to enhance benchmarking practices in the AI research community.

articles.title: How Endava is redesigning software delivery around AI agents
articles.summary: Endava is leveraging AI agents, including ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex, to enhance software delivery and automate workflows. The company aims to foster an AI-native culture throughout its operations.

articles.title: TSMC struggles to keep up with AI demand: ‘We can only support so much’
articles.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) is facing challenges in meeting the high demand for semiconductors from American customers, despite ongoing factory expansions in the US. CEO C.C. Wei acknowledged the limitations in their capacity to support this demand during a recent shareholder meeting.

articles.title: Meta steals a tactic from Tesla and builds data centers in tents
articles.summary: Meta is reportedly constructing data centers using tents as a cost-saving measure to reduce its significant operational expenses. This approach mirrors a strategy previously employed by Tesla to manage infrastructure costs.
